title: Homemade Mac N Cheese Dry Mix
summary: A pantry jar of cheddar cheese powder, nutritional yeast, and spices that stands in for boxed mac and cheese. Whisk the mix into any drained pasta with a splash of water or milk for a creamy sauce in minutes.
servings: 1 pint jar (32 tablespoons); about 10–11 uses at 3 tbsp each

ingredient_groups.group: To make one batch of mac and cheese

items.name: pasta
items.notes: macaroni for example; any shape or type works

items.original_text: up to 3 tbsp water or milk, one tbsp at a time
items.name: water or milk
items.notes: up to 3 tbsp; add one tbsp at a time until creamy

items: Add every dry ingredient to a pint jar.
Seal the jar, shake until evenly blended, and label it.
Store in a cool, dark place.
Cook 8 oz pasta (macaroni works) as the package directs, then drain. Stir in 3 tbsp of the dry mix, then add up to 3 tbsp water or milk one tablespoon at a time, mixing until creamy.

notes: Turn it into a fuller plate by stirring in cooked protein or vegetables at the end.
In a sealed jar kept cool, dark, and dry, flavor holds for about 6 months; moisture leads to clumping and spoilage.
Always scoop with a dry spoon.
Any noodle works: protein pasta, veggie noodles, gluten-free pasta, or whatever is on hand.

flags.text: Source recipe card lists Diet as Dairy-Free, but the mix includes dry milk powder and butter powder (dairy). Cheddar cheese powder is also typically dairy.
Blog body says one batch makes about 12 servings; the card yield is 32 tablespoons at 3 tbsp per use (~10–11 uses). Using the card yield.
Source step text has a typo: "Mix until until creamy." Reworded without the double "until."
Gluten-Free and Dairy-Free claims depend on the powder brands and the pasta chosen; not independently verified.
